mainEntity.name: How long do flexible dentures typically last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Flexible dentures may last several years with appropriate care, though their lifespan can vary depending on individual factors such as oral health, chewing habits, and maintenance routine. For a more detailed look at expected timelines, see our guide on how long flexible dentures last. Over time, natural changes in the jawbone and gum tissue may affect the fit, and the material itself may show signs of wear. Regular dental reviews allow your dentist to monitor the condition of your dentures and advise whether adjustment, relining, or replacement may be appropriate. It is difficult to give a precise timeframe, as each patient's situation is different.

mainEntity.name: Can flexible dentures be repaired if they crack or tear?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repairing flexible dentures can be more complex than repairing traditional acrylic dentures because the thermoplastic nylon material requires specialist techniques and equipment. Standard denture repair kits available over the counter are generally designed for acrylic and may not bond effectively with flexible materials. If your flexible denture develops damage, it is best to consult your dental professional, who can assess the extent of the issue and advise whether a repair is possible or whether a replacement may be more appropriate.

mainEntity.name: Are flexible dentures suitable for everyone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Flexible dentures are not suitable for every patient or every clinical situation. Their suitability depends on factors including the number and position of missing teeth, the health of the remaining teeth and gums, the condition of the jawbone, and the patient's individual needs and preferences. A clinical examination is necessary to determine whether flexible dentures are an appropriate option. Your dentist can discuss the various types of dentures available and help you understand which may be most suitable for your circumstances.

mainEntity.name: Do flexible dentures stain more easily than other types?

acceptedAnswer.text: The nylon material used in flexible dentures can be more prone to absorbing stains than traditional acrylic, particularly if exposed to strongly coloured food and drink such as tea, coffee, red wine, or curry over a prolonged period. Using the correct cleaning products and maintaining a consistent daily cleaning routine can help minimise staining. Professional cleaning during routine dental appointments can also help maintain the appearance of your dentures. If discolouration becomes significant, your dentist can advise on the best course of action.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to sleep while wearing flexible dentures?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is generally recommended that dentures — including flexible ones — are removed at night. This allows the gum tissues to rest and recover from the pressure of wearing the denture during the day. Removing dentures overnight also supports better oral hygiene, as it reduces the risk of bacterial and fungal build-up on the denture surface and the underlying tissues. Storing them in a suitable soaking solution overnight helps keep the material hydrated and in good condition. Your dentist can provide personalised advice based on your specific situation.

mainEntity.name: Can I adjust flexible dentures myself at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is not advisable to attempt to adjust flexible dentures yourself. Bending, cutting, or modifying the denture at home can cause irreversible damage to the material and may result in a poor fit that irritates the gums or affects your bite. If your dentures feel uncomfortable or no longer fit properly, a dental professional has the appropriate tools and expertise to make precise adjustments safely. Wearing an ill-fitting denture without seeking professional advice may lead to sore spots, tissue irritation, or other oral health concerns.
